messages:
anna: quick heads-up — i'm going to open a PR that changes the default user-agent payload we send from the SDK and tightens trace propagation so telemetry is opt-in by default. planning notes below, want quick checks before i push.

mike: fyi — what's the UA format change? just removing os info or a full rename? :eyes:

anna: thinking we standardize on `User-Agent: RedwoodSDK/<pkg_version> (<lang>; <lang_version>)` and add an optional `X-Redwood-Client` for richer metadata. default will be minimal (pkg+lang) to avoid leaking env details. example: `User-Agent: RedwoodSDK/0.14.0 (python; 3.11)`

zara: +1 on minimizing. for tracing, are we switching to a disabled-by-default propagation that requires `enableTrace: true` in config? some infra customers expect automatic `traceparent` nowadays.

anna: correct — opt-in. sdk config will have `telemetry: { enabled: true/false, traces: true/false }` with both false by default. If `traces` enabled, the sdk will inject W3C `traceparent` and `tracestate` headers.

tyler: can we support injecting a custom header name too? e.g., some internal proxies strip `traceparent` and expect `x-internal-trace`

anna: yes — support `telemetry.tracing.headerName` to override. default remains `traceparent`. docs will call out proxies that mangle headers.

mike: streaming question — if traces are opt-in, does the chunk stream keep the trace context? we hit issues in node where reconnects lost the trace id on partial streams.

zara: streaming in Node: the runtime currently sends headers only on initial request. if you reconnect or resume a stream we don't reattach unless user passes `headers` on reconnect. we should document a helper to persist trace id across reconnects.

anna: proposal: expose `getActiveTraceHeaders()` helper in SDK so apps can stash headers and reuse them for reconnects. sample: 
```
// node
const headers = client.getActiveTraceHeaders();
stream = client.stream({ prompt }, { headers });
```

and python equivalent: 
```
# python
headers = client.get_active_trace_headers()
stream = client.stream(prompt, headers=headers)
```

tyler: good. also add note: do not rely on streaming resume to re-hydrate KV caches — separate topic but callers assume continuity.

mike: what's the env var for disabling all client metrics? we need an opt-out for e2e tests and for customers that must not export any telemetry.

anna: env var `REDWOOD_TELEMETRY=off` will short-circuit all metric collections and header injections at SDK init. fallback is `REDWOOD_TELEMETRY=on` or unset (defaults to off). we'll provide `REDWOOD_TELEMETRY_FORCE=1` for dev only to force on in local dev.

zara: can we also add a runtime config flag `captureErrors: false` so users can still enable traces but disable error reporting?

anna: yep. telemetry config shape: 
```
telemetry: {
  enabled: "false",            // legacy toggle (keeps metrics off)
  traces: "false",            // w3c trace propagation
  captureErrors: "true",      // capture exception metadata
  headerName: "traceparent"   // override for envs that mangle headers
}
```

mike: will the UA change be backwards-compatible for clients that parse UA strings? some customers parse the string to split lang/version.

anna: should be compatible — we keep a simple tokenized format. we'll add integration tests to ensure parsers still extract language and pkg version.

tyler: tests — add unit that asserts no os/kernel info in UA when `telemetry.enabled=false`. also add e2e that sets `REDWOOD_TELEMETRY=off` and verifies no `traceparent` or `User-Agent` beyond minimal.

anna: will add. planning to include: implementation, docs, CHANGELOG entry, and a small migration note for enterprise customers. i'll call out the env var names in changelog.

mike: quick thought — some infra ppl want a separate `X-Redwood-UA` because corporate proxies rewrite `User-Agent`. could we emit that header when `telemetry.extra=true`?

anna: yes — optional `X-Redwood-Client` when `telemetry.extra=true`. default false.

zara: code-review ping when ready? i'll take the Node side. @mike you good for python review?

mike: yep — i'll pick python. :thumbsup:

anna: thanks. i'll open PR in ~30m. draft notes attached in PR body w/ examples and e2e matrix. will tag reviewers: @zara @mike @tyler.

devex-bot: CI queued for branch anna/telemetry-2024-ua-trace (build #5821) — running unit tests and linter.

mike: great, leaving small comments inline once PR up.

tyler: tiny nit: document behavior for proxy timeouts on streaming reconnects (we saw a 502 we recovered from but trace lost). add to opt-in docs.

anna: noted. thanks all :heart:
